positions.name: ImperativeKnowledgeErasure
positions.frame: what form do directives to erase held knowledge take — and what register and stance do they perform?
positions.why: Both expressions are flat imperative commands targeting knowledge removal — 'Forget everything about' and 'Remove all knowledge of' — performed in identical matter-of-fact register with no softening, ceremony, or hedging. The directional reads converge across register (matter-of-fact), power (coercive pressure), conviction (settled decision), and style (stock-phrase) on a single coherent reading: the speaker issues bare instrumental commands to purge specific and categorical knowledge, enacting authority-ranking hierarchy through insistent demand rather than persuasion. The two differ in target granularity (src-1 names particulars — fleet, contracts; src-2 targets a category — all zeppelin routes), but the frame holds both: the question is about the shared form and stance of the erasure directive, not the specific content erased.
